title: Sample: Pair With Target Sum
statement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.
Each input has exactly one answer. Return the two indices in any order.
hint: For each number x you need target - x. How can you check in O(1) whether you have already seen it?
approach: Walk the array once and keep a map from value to index. Before storing nums[i], look up target - nums[i]; if it is in the map, you have the pair. One pass works because the earlier partner is always in the map when you reach the later one.
followups: What if the array is sorted? (two pointers, O(1) space)
What if you must return all pairs without duplicates?

title: Sample: Valid Brackets
statement: Given a string s of the characters ()[]{}, return true if every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket in the right order.
hint: The most recent unclosed bracket must be closed first. Which data structure gives you the most recent item?
approach: Push opening brackets on a stack. For a closing bracket, the top of the stack must be the matching opener; pop it. At the end the stack must be empty. A stack fits because brackets nest: last opened, first closed.
followups: How would you report the position of the first error?
Can you do it in O(1) space if there is only one bracket type?

title: Sample: Merge Intervals
statement: Given an array of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return the merged list sorted by start.
hint: If the intervals were sorted by start, where could an overlap with the current interval come from?
approach: Sort by start. Keep the last merged interval; if the next one starts before or at its end, extend the end; otherwise start a new interval. After sorting, an interval can only overlap the one just before it in the output.
complexity: O(n log n) time for the sort, O(n) space for the output
followups: How would you insert one new interval into an already merged list in O(n)?
What if the intervals arrive as a stream?
